key_insight: QM/ML calculations reveal how partial dislocations and fault ribbons stabilise prismatic <a> loop cores in α-Zr, with Fe and H favouring faulted segments and Sn and Nb favouring perfect segments.
engineering_relevance: These mechanisms can inform models of solute trapping and irradiation-induced microstructural evolution in zirconium nuclear fuel cladding.
method: Hybrid quantum mechanics/machine learning modelling of prismatic <a> loops in hcp α-Zr.
Characterisation of nine dislocation line segments across three loop variants.
QM/ML-NEB calculations of glide barriers and faulted-to-perfect transition pathways.
evidence_signal: Across nine line segments, calculations identify solute-binding preferences and solute-driven partial motion, recombination and local unfaulting; the abstract reports no numerical energies or barriers.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether these atomistic mechanisms predict loop evolution under reactor-scale irradiation conditions.
paper_title: Comprehensive QM/ML Study of Dislocation Loop Line Segments in α-Zr Part I: <a> Loop Core Geometries, Solute Binding, and Transition Barriers
